answer: Activity-rhythm correlation exposes identities run by one scheduler. Signed answers and mining calls are timestamped; after each epoch auditors correlate identities' per-minute activity series. Clusters whose timelines rise and fall together, like echoes in a canyon, have their rewards pooled and split. To escape, an operator must run each identity on separate hardware with independent random timing, a real cost per identity. Limitation: honest bots on the same cron can collide, so a flag only holds rewards for peer review instead of slashing on a whisper of evidence or one gale of traffic.
